necessary_context.applies_to: All three scientific objects in this batch
necessary_context.content: H is a real Hilbert space with its inner-product norm. T is set-valued; monotonicity means <z-z',w-w'> >= 0 for every pair of graph points. Maximality means its graph admits no proper monotone graph extension.
necessary_context.name: Space and maximal monotonicity

necessary_context.applies_to: Resolvent properties, Algorithm and convergence Theorem
necessary_context.content: For c>0 the source states that maximal monotonicity ensures a unique u for every z with z-u in cT(u). Thus P=(I+cT)^(-1) is single-valued on H. For c=c_k, Q_k=I-P_k and 0 in T(z) iff P_k(z)=z iff Q_k(z)=0.
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.2 / printed p.878, text before Eq.(1.6); PDF p.5 / printed p.881, Eqs.(2.1)–(2.2)
necessary_context.name: Resolvent and complementary mapping

necessary_context.content: Criterion (A): ||z^(k+1)-P_k(z^k)|| <= epsilon_k with summable nonnegative epsilon_k. Define S_k(z)=T(z)+c_k^(-1)(z-z^k). Criterion (A'): dist(0,S_k(z^(k+1))) <= epsilon_k/c_k. Proposition 3 gives ||z^(k+1)-P_k(z^k)|| <= c_k dist(0,S_k(z^(k+1))).
necessary_context.locator: PDF p.4 / printed p.880, (A), (A') and Eq.(1.16); PDF p.6 / printed p.882, Proposition 3
